mathviz ships two ways from one source tree. Both give you the same `window.VM`, the same CSS, and the same self-installing behaviour.

## Quarto site, book or document

```sh
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz
```

This copies the extension into `_extensions/apurvanakade/mathviz/` in your project. Enable it project-wide in `_quarto.yml`, or per page in front matter:

```yaml
filters:
  - mathviz
```

The filter adds four things to every HTML page's `<head>`, **in this order**:

1. `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjs@15.2.0/lib/browser/math.js">` -- the global `math`
2. `<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.35.2.min.js">` -- the global `Plotly`
3. `mathviz.js`, copied into `site_libs/quarto-contrib/mathviz-<version>/`
4. `mathviz.css`, alongside it

The order matters: `mathviz.js` patches `Plotly.newPlot` the moment it runs, so Plotly must already be there. Both vendor tags come from CDNs (they're pinned to the versions the library is tested against); the bundle is served from your own site.

### Options

All optional, under a `mathviz:` key in `_quarto.yml` or a page's front matter:

```yaml
mathviz:
  plotly: false             # your pages draw with D3/canvas/Plot -- skip Plotly
  mathjs: false             # ...or math.js. Either also accepts a URL string
  css: false                # bring your own stylesheet
  referrer: same-origin     # emit <meta name="referrer"> ahead of the CDN tags
```

| Key | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `plotly` | `true` (default), `false`, or a URL | Whether to add the Plotly tag, and from where. With `false` the Plotly patch is a silent no-op and the `VM.plotting` theme functions still work for Observable Plot. |
| `mathjs` | `true` (default), `false`, or a URL | Whether to add the math.js tag, and from where. `VM.expressions.*` take the instance as an argument, so a page that loads math.js another way passes that. |
| `css` | `true` (default) or `false` | Whether to add `mathviz.css`. With `false` you supply the `--vm-*` tokens and the `ojs-*` rules yourself -- see [Theming](theming.qmd). |
| `referrer` | a [referrer policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name/referrer) string | Emits `<meta name="referrer" content="…">` **before** the CDN tags, so the third-party origins don't see a page's path or query string -- which on a math page is the reader's own input. Visual Math Lab uses `same-origin`. |

### Versions and updating

```sh
quarto update apurvanakade/mathviz            # latest tag
quarto update apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.2     # a specific tag
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.2        # pin at install time
```

The version names the `site_libs/quarto-contrib/mathviz-<version>/` folder in your rendered output, which is what invalidates a browser's cached copy when you upgrade.

### Trying a local checkout

To test a change to the library in your own project before it's published:

```sh
quarto add /path/to/mathviz --no-prompt
```

A local directory is accepted; Quarto copies `_extensions/mathviz/` in. Re-run after each `npm run build` in the library. A **symlink** at `_extensions/mathviz` is not discovered -- Quarto checks `isDirectory()` on the raw directory entry.

## Any other web page

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.2/dist/mathviz.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjs@15.2.0/lib/browser/math.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.35.2.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.2/dist/mathviz.js"></script>
```

- Load **Plotly before `mathviz.js`**. The patch runs when the bundle loads and again on `DOMContentLoaded`; if Plotly arrives later than both (a dynamic import), call [`VM.plotting.installPlotlyPatch()`](reference/plotting.qmd#installPlotlyPatch) yourself.
- `dist/mathviz.js` is a plain concatenation of the source files -- readable, un-minified, ~170 kB with its documentation comments. A stack trace in your browser points at a recognizable file.
- Pin the tag in the URL. jsDelivr also serves `@main`, but a tag is what you can reason about.
- Without Quarto and Observable Inputs, some CSS has nothing to attach to; the [markup contract](markup.qmd#host-markup) says what degrades and what doesn't.

## What needs what

Nothing here imports anything. Where a function needs a library, it takes it as an argument or finds it on `window`.

| | Needs |
|---|---|
| `VM.expressions.*` (except `makeRational`), `VM.numerical.polynomialFit` | a math.js instance, **passed as the first argument** |
| `VM.numerical.*`, `VM.sampling.*`, `VM.filters.*`, `VM.distributions.*`, `VM.discreteMath.*` | nothing |
| `VM.plotting.colors / colorway / alpha / themeName / onThemeChange / configure / subscript / paddedRange / plotOptions` | nothing (a `document` to read tokens from; sensible fallbacks without) |
| `VM.plotting.layout / config / hoverLabel / emptyState / themePatch` | nothing -- they build plain objects. You need Plotly to *use* them, of course |
| `VM.plotting.autoResize` | `ResizeObserver` (returns `null` without); safe when Plotly is absent |
| `VM.plotting.installPlotlyPatch / fullscreenButton` | `window.Plotly` |
| `VM.plotting.svgAspectRatio / figureBounds`, `VM.ui.clampOverlayOffset / overlayStorageKey / playbackDuration / playbackFrame` | nothing -- pure helpers |
| `VM.ui.legendOverlay` | nothing -- plain DOM. It *implements* Observable's view contract; it doesn't require Observable |
| `VM.ui.renderTable` | htl's `html` tag, passed in. Emits Bootstrap table classes |
| `VM.ui.applyExampleParams` | views that follow Observable Inputs' `value` + `"input"` protocol |
| slider playback, draggable legend, SVG fullscreen button, slider fill | nothing -- self-installing on the [markup](markup.qmd) they look for |
